title: Figure 5 | Cancer-type-associated variation in TCGA bulk expression across previously defined CGT candidate score sets.
alt: Six-panel TCGA bulk-expression analysis showing cohort QC, pooled score transformations, a TCGA-fitted PCA with all 33 cancer-type centroids, relative cancer-type profiles, in-sample variance fractions, and residual score correlations.
caption_markdown_lines: **Figure 5 | Cancer-type-associated variation in TCGA bulk expression across previously defined CGT candidate score sets.** Fifteen candidate score definitions were imported from the frozen upstream CGT registry, where gene membership was derived from prior perturbational analyses rather than TCGA cancer-type labels. This establishes dataset separation, not statistical independence, orthogonality, external validation, or causal identifiability. The packaged Figure 5 materials document the transformations applied to the frozen raw-score matrix but not the formula used to map TCGA expression and registry entries to those raw scores; the figure is therefore reproducible from the supplied score matrix but not independently reconstructable from expression and the registry alone.

**a, Bulk TCGA cohort after expression QC.** The input comprised 9,359 TCGA tumor-derived bulk-expression samples. Fifty-seven samples with median expression below 2.5 across the retained score-gene union were excluded, leaving 9,302 samples from 9,302 patients and 33 corrected cancer-type categories. The retained cohort comprises 9,128 primary-tumor samples, 173 primary blood-derived cancer samples, and one recurrent-tumor sample. The 15 candidate score sets contain 1,876 recovered gene memberships spanning 970 unique genes; 595 of those genes (61.3%) occur in at least two score sets. Twenty of the 57 exclusions were liver hepatocellular carcinoma samples, so exclusion was not uniform across cancer types.

**b, Within-cohort transforms reduce shared score dependence.** For each matrix, PCA was fitted after separately standardizing all 15 score columns. PC1 accounted for 83.0% of standardized-score variance in the raw matrix, 33.2% after subtracting each sample's mean across its 15 scores, and 32.2% after pooled leave-one-axis-out residualization. Mean absolute Spearman correlation across the 105 unique score pairs was 0.753, 0.279, and 0.265, respectively. For each score, pooled leave-one-axis-out residualization regressed the raw score once across all 9,302 samples on an intercept, the z-standardized mean of the other 14 scores, and z-standardized sample-median expression across the retained score genes; the plotted value is the OLS residual. The 15 same-cohort models accounted for 31.4%–98.6% of their respective raw-score variance. These reductions are expected properties of the transformations, not evidence of biological independence, successful deconfounding, or out-of-sample validation.

**c, TCGA-fitted PCA of pooled residual scores.** PCA was fitted after standardizing all 15 pooled leave-one-axis-out residual scores within the same 9,302 TCGA samples. PC1 and PC2 accounted for 32.2% and 14.3%, respectively. The neutral cloud contains every retained sample; the 33 equally sized blue markers are same-sample cancer-type means, and the adjacent labels report all cancer-type abbreviations and post-QC sample counts. Samples, rather than cancer types, were equally weighted when fitting PCA, so larger cancer types exert greater influence. The centroids are descriptive same-cohort summaries, not held-out predictions; component signs are arbitrary and carry no directional biological meaning.

**d, Within-cancer-type relative mean score profiles.** All 33 cancer types are ordered alphabetically. The 12 source-named score sets are ordered by their raw in-sample between-cancer-type variance fraction, matching their numbering in panel e; one exploratory and two unresolved source labels are not included in this panel. Each cell is the cancer-type mean pooled residual score followed by centering and sample-standardization across the 12 displayed scores within that cancer-type row. Color therefore indicates only relative prominence within one row: absolute magnitudes and colors are not comparable across cancer types. Group sizes range from 36 to 1,092, and no uncertainty is displayed.
**e, In-sample between-cancer-type variance fraction.** For score (j), the sample-weighted descriptive statistic is

Open circles show raw scores and filled diamonds show pooled leave-one-axis-out residual scores for all 15 score sets, ordered by raw \(\eta^2_{\mathrm{in}}\). The raw values range from 0.249 to 0.453 and the residual values from 0.256 to 0.570. Residualization increases the statistic for seven scores and decreases it for eight; the unresolved source label has the largest residual value (0.570). These estimates are unadjusted, sample-weighted, and calculated and evaluated in the same cohort, without confidence intervals, permutation calibration, cancer-type balancing, or cross-validation. They measure cancer-type-associated between-group heterogeneity; they do not identify a cancer-type effect or a lineage mechanism.

**f, Residual score dependence remains.** The lower triangle shows pairwise Spearman correlations among all 15 pooled residual scores in the same order as panel e; the diagonal and duplicated upper triangle are omitted. Mean absolute off-diagonal correlation is 0.265 and the maximum is 0.871, between the T-cell/antigen-receptor and mixed interferon/chromatin score sets. Those two sets share 56 recovered genes (Jaccard similarity 0.709); the chromatin/cytokine and cytokine/JAK–STAT sets share 38 genes (0.422). Score dependence can reflect shared gene membership, coexpression, RNA content, tumor purity, cellular composition, technical variation, or coordinated biology. Residualization therefore does not make the candidate scores orthogonal or independent.

**Interpretive and provenance limitations.** All panels are descriptive analyses of one harmonized bulk-expression cohort. No direct cancer-type-label term is used in residualization or PCA, but expression QC, residualization, standardization, PCA, centroid construction, ordering, and evaluation are all performed within the same TCGA cohort. Bulk scores mix malignant, immune, and stromal expression; cancer type co-varies with tissue of origin, tumor purity, cellular composition, sex, batch, and other cohort structure. No matched random-gene-set baseline, independent cohort, study-held-out reconstruction, single-cell localization, patient-outcome analysis, intervention, or causal contrast is tested. The archived source notebook has SHA-256 `51dee19a0791dfada00fc021649eb19b87789edab728b7afec5be576c25c84f5`, whereas a later Drive inventory recorded a larger same-named notebook with SHA-256 `72d1efabe3dd8c0447817dedae3d6004b47374065eb90f83f9179ad8d525fb81`; that version mismatch could not be reconciled. The revised figure is reproducible from the frozen score matrices and audited tables supplied in the release, but the upstream raw-score construction is not independently reconstructable from the packaged expression metadata and registry alone. The figure therefore does not establish CGT specificity, tumor-cell-intrinsic programs, transportability, mechanisms, or universal constraints.
accessible_description_markdown_lines: Six panels describe 9,302 retained TCGA tumor-derived bulk-expression samples from 33 corrected cancer-type categories using 15 candidate CGT-derived score definitions imported from prior perturbational work. Panel a reports that 57 of 9,359 input samples failed an expression threshold; the 15 score sets use 970 unique recovered genes, most of which are reused across score sets. Panel b shows strong dependence among raw scores: PC1 of a standardized PCA accounts for 83.0% of variance and mean absolute pairwise Spearman correlation is 0.753. Per-sample centering and full-cohort leave-one-axis-out regression against the mean of the other scores and sample-median expression reduce those summaries to approximately 32% and 0.265, but this is an expected property of the pooled transforms rather than proof that confounding was removed. Panel c is a PCA fitted within TCGA: a pale cloud shows all samples, while all 33 cancer-type centroids are labelled in collision-free side gutters. Panel d shows row-standardized cancer-type means for 12 named scores; colors convey only within-row relative prominence. Panel e shows sample-weighted, in-sample between-cancer-type variance fractions for all 15 raw and residual scores, including the previously omitted exploratory and unresolved labels. Panel f shows that residual correlations remain as large as 0.871. These patterns can reflect tissue of origin, tumor purity, immune and stromal composition, gene-set overlap, technical variation, or coordinated biology. They do not demonstrate orthogonal axes, independent validation, tumor-cell-intrinsic state, transportability, mechanism, or causality.
responsive_presentation_requirement: Keep the full composite on desktop. At the established narrow breakpoint, replace it with panels a–f in semantic order. Fit panel a to the container; use keyboard- and touch-accessible component-level horizontal scrollers with minimum display widths of 640 px for b, 680 px for c, 820 px for d, 620 px for e, and 680 px for f. Panel images have empty alt text because the figure-level alt and accessible description carry the semantics. Retain the full-resolution SVG affordance and prevent page-level horizontal overflow.
